newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds sell off at close on weak U.S.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds sell off at close on weak U.S.

text.p: Canadian bonds sold off at the close on Thursday, following the U.S. market lower as fears of a U.S. interest rate hike increased ahead of Friday's closely watched U.S. jobs data.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.57 to C$110.58 to yield 7.103 percent against U.S. 30-year benchmark, which fell 22/32 to yield 6.88 percent. The spread totaled 22 basis points.
"It's on the back of the U.S. here," said Lehman Brothers vice-president Michael Gregory. "There's the growing worries of U.S. tightening."
"That's beginning to swirl ahead of U.S. employment numbers," Gregory said.

Investors are anticipating February's non-farm payrolls on Friday. Economists polled by Reuters estimated that on average U.S. non-farm jobs swelled by 230,000 in February, after growth of 271,000 in January.
Gregory forecast that rate-hike jitters will intensify if February's growth is higher than 250,000 jobs, indicating that inflation is on the rise.
February's U.S. unemployment rate will also be released.
